content.text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine bearing a 3-nitrophenyl group at C4, methyl groups at C2 and C6, and two ester groups at C3 and C5.

Each ester is an OCH2CH2O-nPr group. The "nPr" label is n-propyl, so each side chain is C(=O)OCCOCCC.

Ring atoms, with the NH at the top:
- N1 is bonded to C2 (methyl) and C6 (methyl).
- C2=C3, and C3 carries the left ester.
- C4 is the sp3 carbon carrying the aryl group.
- C5=C6, and C5 carries the right ester.

Aryl ring: the carbon attached to C4 has the nitro-bearing carbon as its meta neighbour. In the drawing the attachment carbon is at (645, 845). Going around the ring, the next atom is (530, 857), then (483, 965), which bears the NO2. The NO2 carbon is therefore separated from the attachment carbon by one carbon, so it is meta.

SMILES: CCCOCCOC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OCCOCCC)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1
